cards.explanation: The answer is that the LORD had appeared to David there. The text says Solomon built on Mount Moriah, "…where the LORD had appeared to his father David." (2 Chronicles 3:1) So this spot was already special before one stone got stacked. I like a builder who starts with the place God already showed up.

The answer is David. The text says this was "…the place that David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite." (2 Chronicles 3:1) So Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, is building on ground his father got ready. I know a little about being prepared for a job I didn't see coming, friends.

The answer is wing, wing to wing, friends. One wing of the first cherub is five cubits long and touches the wall of the temple, and its other wing is five cubits long and touches the wing of the other cherub. (2 Chronicles 3:11) The second cherub's wings measure the same and touch the wall and the first cherub's wing. (2 Chronicles 3:12) Together the total wingspan is twenty cubits. (2 Chronicles 3:13)

The answer is True. Each cherub has two wings of five cubits, so the total wingspan is twenty cubits (2 Chronicles 3:11-13). The Most Holy Place is twenty cubits wide (2 Chronicles 3:8). One wing touches one wall, the other cherub's wing touches the opposite wall, and the room is covered, wall to wall. That's some tidy measuring, friends.

The answer is cherubim. Solomon "…made the veil of blue, purple, and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim woven into it." (2 Chronicles 3:14) So you've got cherubim on the walls, cherubim in the Most Holy Place and cherubim in the thread. The man had a theme, friends.

The answer is True. The text says Solomon set up the pillars in front of the temple, and "The pillar on the south he named Jachin, and the pillar on the north he named Boaz." (2 Chronicles 3:17) These aren't just big columns. They've got names, bakers. I was carved with a name too, so I appreciate it.

The answer is Jachin and Boaz. Solomon named the south pillar Jachin and the north pillar Boaz. (2 Chronicles 3:17) Two names, two pillars, one on each side. Say them out loud a couple of times, friends, they're fun.

The answer is oxen, twelve of them. "The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east." (2 Chronicles 4:4) Their hindquarters pointed to the center, and the Sea rested on them. That's a lot of oxen holding up one very big bowl, bakers.

The answer is the priests. Verse 6 says the parts of the burnt offering were rinsed in the ten basins, "…but the priests used the Sea for washing." (2 Chronicles 4:6) So there were two sets of washing, each for its own use. The Sea was the priests' tub, friends.

The answer is False. Solomon made ten gold lampstands, but he placed them in the temple, "…five on the south side and five on the north." (2 Chronicles 4:7) They were split down the middle, not all on the north. That's an even split, friends.

The answer is bowls, a hundred of them, all gold. The text says, "He also made a hundred gold bowls." (2 Chronicles 4:8) That comes right after the ten tables he placed in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. Bowls it is, friends.

The answer is that no one could figure out the weight, and the text says so plainly. Solomon made all these articles in such great abundance "…that the weight of the bronze could not be determined." (2 Chronicles 4:18) The pile was so big that no one could settle on a weight for it. I can't even get my cookie dough to the right pound, friends.

The answer is the Bread of the Presence. Solomon made "the tables on which was placed the Bread of the Presence…" (2 Chronicles 4:19) Those tables had a very specific job. A table with a purpose, friends, I respect that.

The answer is False. The lampstands of pure gold and their lamps were "…to burn in front of the inner sanctuary as prescribed…" (2 Chronicles 4:20) The large court is mentioned earlier, with bronze doors (2 Chronicles 4:9). Different spot, bakers.
